Definition: {to pluck up (especially by the roots); specifically, to hamstring; figuratively, to exterminate}
BiblicalUsage: In Daniel's vision of the four beasts, a little horn comes up among ten horns, and three of the first horns are plucked up by the roots before it. The word is that uprooting, power torn out to make room for a smaller, louder power.
TheologicalSignificance: Horns that look immovable can be plucked up overnight, and the vision says to watch what grows in their place.
